papers.container_title_hint: The 37th International Conference on Software Engineering and Knowledge Engineering, SEKE 2025, KSIR Virtual Conference Center, USA, September 29-30, 2025.
papers.abstract: Label Propagation Algorithm (LPA) is a method of predicting node labels on graph structured data by utilizing the correlation relationships between nodes.It is widely used in scenarios such as community detection and risk transmission analysis.Current LPA is mainly executed on a single data source, and the data value of individual participants is usually limited.With the increasing demand of data applications in multiple participants, integrating multi-party data for label propagation is a promising research direction.In multi-party scenarios, each participant usually needs to avoid exposing their own private data to the other party.How to enable multiple participant to better execute LPA while protecting their own privacy data, and achieve effective integration and utilization of multi-party data value, is a problem that needs to be studied.This article proposes a privacy preserving cross-domain label propagation algorithm (PPCD-LPA), which uses a secure intersection protocol based on RSA+HASH algorithm to achieve secure matching of intersection nodes in the graph structured data of each participating party.A secure label aggregation algorithm based on semi-homomorphic encryption and a combination of random numbers is designed to calculate and update the labels of each node, thereby protecting the sensitive information of each party.This article tested and validated PPCD-LPA on multiple datasets, and the experimental results showed that PPCD-LPA can run securely and correctly among multiple parties, achieve the same model effect as plaintext cross-domain label propagation algorithm and has engineering practicality.

papers.abstract: Semantic conflicts in branch merging occur when merged code violates specifications from one or both branches.These conflicts are often subtle and can lead to serious runtime errors such as crashes or data corruption.Existing detection methods fail to achieve both high precision and recall: Static analysis-based methods ensure high recall but lack precision, whereas dynamic execution-based methods provide better precision but struggle with recall due to limited test coverage.To better understand such conflicts, we first conduct an empirical study on a real-world merge dataset and identify four common conflict patterns.These patterns reveal key characteristics of semantic conflicts and serve as guidance for automated detection.Based on these insights, we propose ConflictLens, a two-stage LLM-based method that combines static analysis and dynamic execution to balance precision and recall.First, LLMs are guided by few-shot and chain-of-thought prompting using the patterns to localize conflicts statically.Then, conflicts are dynamically verified with LLM-generated targeted tests, refined through execution feedback.Evaluated on 85 real-world merge scenarios, ConflictLens achieves 0.91 precision and 0.76 recall, outperforming static and dynamic baselines.Ablation studies demonstrate the contribution and synergy of each component.Cross-LLM evaluations confirm robustness, with DeepSeek-R1 performing best and cost-efficient models like GPT-4o-Mini still competitive.

papers.abstract: JavaScript, as one of the most popular front-end languages today, has inspired the widespread development and use of various JavaScript libraries.However, the issue of "unused modules reducing program efficiency" has persisted.To address this, the concept of pure functions was introduced to JavaScript programming, with software tools available to remove unused modules from JavaScript project bundles, thereby optimizing the code.Nonetheless, such tools require access to complete source code to accurately identify pure functions in JavaScript, which is often impractical when certain parts of the source code are unavailable.This study focuses on analyzing JavaScript function call code rather than the complete code, using machine learning methods to determine whether a called function is pure.This is the first study to apply machine learning methods to research JavaScript pure functions.The main contributions of this paper include: ( 1) constructing a dataset comprising both pure and unpure function calls; (2) proposing four research methods: a traditional machine learning model based on character features, an LSTM model based on AST structural features, a CNN model based on large model explanations and BERT tokenization, and full fine-tuning of CodeBERT on code features.Experimental results show that the LSTM model based on AST structural features achieved the highest accuracy of 0.9787, though with significant variability, while CodeBERT fine-tuning reached an accuracy of 0.9552 with more stable results.The research results indicate that introducing machine learning methods into the detection of JavaScript pure functions is entirely feasible.

papers.abstract: Project-based learning is a critical component of software engineering education, particularly in senior design or capstone courses where students collaborate on real-world projects.However, evaluating individual contributions and maintaining healthy team dynamics remain persistent challenges.Issues such as social loafing, uneven workload distribution, and subjective grading hinder both student outcomes and instructional effectiveness.This paper presents Project Pulse, a webbased platform designed to enhance transparency, accountability, and feedback in team-based software projects.By automating weekly activity reporting and structured peer evaluations, Project Pulse provides real-time insights into individual and team performance, allowing instructors to detect problems early and assess contributions more fairly.The platform has been deployed in a year-long senior design course involving 50 students across 8 teams.Survey results indicate improved student accountability, enhanced collaboration, and reduced administrative overhead for instructors.Project Pulse is open source, publicly accessible at https://projectpulse.team, and demonstrates how software engineering tools can be applied to improve software engineering education itself.A short demo video showcasing key features is available at https://youtu.be/ASaR3UdrwKg.

papers.title: SGTest: A Semantics-Guided Framework for LLM-Driven Unit Test Generation
papers.container_title_hint: The 37th International Conference on Software Engineering and Knowledge Engineering, SEKE 2025, KSIR Virtual Conference Center, USA, September 29-30, 2025.
papers.abstract: Unit testing is crucial for ensuring software quality, yet manually writing test cases remains a time-consuming and error-prone task.While traditional test generation approaches rely on program analysis and heuristics, and recent methods leverage large language models (LLMs), both face persistent challenges such as complex class instantiation, encapsulated state access, and low test execution rates.In this paper, we propose SGTest, a novel LLM-driven framework for unit test generation that enhances the large language model's understanding of focal methods and improves the quality of generated test cases through static analysis and iterative repair.SGTest employs a semanticsguided strategy that assists the LLM in constructing class instantiations and accessing or modifying encapsulated states, thereby tackling the first two challenges.Additionally, it integrates static analysis and runtime feedback to iteratively repair generated tests, significantly improving test execution rates.Evaluated on 4,821 focal methods from real-world projects, SGTest achieves 69.59% statement coverage, 55.05% branch coverage, and a 68.90% execution pass rate, substantially outperforming state-ofthe-art approaches.These results demonstrate the effectiveness of SGTest in enhancing both the quality and executability of LLM-generated test cases.

papers.abstract: The Zlus language excels at describing hybrid systems but has limitations in handling uncertainties, such as probabilistic transitions and random failures, in nuclear Instrumentation and Control (I&C) systems.Other languages for modeling uncertainty often choose to discretize the continuous behavior in the system, making it difficult to accurately describe the system.To address this, we propose Stochastic Zlus, a new language integrating probabilistic automata for modeling hybrid systems in uncertain environments.We also developed a quantitative analysis framework and a prototype tool for converting Stochastic Zlus models to NSHA (Networks of Stochastic Hybrid Automata) models supported by UPPAAL-SMC, to support quantitative analysis of stochastic Zlus models using UPPAAL-SMC.Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a case study on a Reactor Protection System (PS), proving that the method is effective in verifying the reliability of the PS in uncertain environments.

papers.title: Substructure Mining Based on Fact Reflection
papers.container_title_hint: The 37th International Conference on Software Engineering and Knowledge Engineering, SEKE 2025, KSIR Virtual Conference Center, USA, September 29-30, 2025.
papers.abstract: Substructure mining serves as a fundamental technique for uncovering key patterns and latent risk within complex networks.Existing methods focus on modeling of topological and semantic information, while neglecting the cross-layer semantic confusion and initial decisions unreliability resulting from intrinsic coupling between them.Faced with that, this study proposes a novel Graph Transformer model based on fact reflection, named RAGphormer, which enhances substructure mining through high-order semantic modeling and dynamic decision reflection.Specifically, we introduce the Sub2Token module, which constructs hierarchical semantic encoding sequences by integrating node-level, substructure-level, and multi-hop neighborhood features.It overcomes the limitations of cross-layer semantic sharing among multi-hop neighborhood nodes, and mitigates the noise caused by multi-hop semantic entanglement.Furthermore, a dynamic decision reflection mechanism is proposed, which constructs substructure fact and counterfactual feature patterns based on an adaptive KMeans clustering algorithm.A dynamic thresholding strategy is employed to identify potentially unreliable predictions, which are then revised based on the discrepancies between corresponding feature patterns.Extensive experiments on two private datasets (ChTech and EnTech) and one public dataset (Cora) demonstrate that RAGphormer outperforms baseline methods across multiple evaluation metrics, achieving an accuracy of up to 98.8%.

papers.container_title_hint: The 37th International Conference on Software Engineering and Knowledge Engineering, SEKE 2025, KSIR Virtual Conference Center, USA, September 29-30, 2025.
papers.abstract: Environmental sustainability is an important priority in the development of intelligent IoT systems.To maintain the precision of the predictive models used in making decisions, the models should be retrained on fresh data that are continuously collected.Continuous data collection leads to maintaining a large amount of training data over time.To overcome this, we propose a framework of federated learners deployed on the Edge that store training data with a sustainable memory footprint.The results of the evaluation of our approach show that the memory footprint of the training data is not perpetually increasing and that the prediction errors made by the sustainable models are not higher than the prediction errors made by the original models.

papers.title: Towards the Impact of Code Readability on Vulnerability Detection: An Empirical Stud
papers.container_title_hint: The 37th International Conference on Software Engineering and Knowledge Engineering, SEKE 2025, KSIR Virtual Conference Center, USA, September 29-30, 2025.
papers.abstract: Vulnerability detection has emerged as a critical component of software security with the growing complexity of software systems.However, the effectiveness of vulnerability detection models is typically evaluated on clean and wellstructured code, despite real-world code often exhibiting significant readability variations.This paper presents a systematic study examining how code readability impacts three types of vulnerability detection approaches: supervised learning-based, fine-tuning-based, and prompt-based methods.Through experiments on two benchmark datasets, we assess the robustness of these methods against seven semantic and syntactic obfuscation rules.Our findings reveal substantial performance degradation under readability challenges, highlighting critical limitations in current detection systems.Specifically, supervised and fine-tuning methods rely more on syntactic information, while prompt-based approaches depend more on semantic understanding.Notably, certain specific types of obfuscation cause more significant declines in model performance.This study provides foundational insights into the relationship between code readability and vulnerability detection effectiveness, offering practical guidance for building more robust models that can better handle realworld code quality variations.The code and data are available at https://anonymous.4open.

papers.title: Verifying the Communication and Security Mechanisms of WAMP
papers.container_title_hint: The 37th International Conference on Software Engineering and Knowledge Engineering, SEKE 2025, KSIR Virtual Conference Center, USA, September 29-30, 2025.
papers.abstract: The Web Application Messaging Protocol (WAMP) is a routed protocol designed to connect components in distributed applications through Publish/Subscribe and Remote Procedure Call messaging patterns.It defines a Basic Profile for core interactions and an Advanced Profile to extend its functionality.With its flexibility, scalability, and ability to support various communication patterns, WAMP has gained significant attention in distributed systems.However, existing studies on the communication and security properties of WAMP remain limited.In this paper, we employ the Communicating Sequential Processes (CSP) to model the two patterns of WAMP formally and verify several properties using Process Analysis Toolkit (PAT), including deadlock-freedom, data reachability, concurrency and ordering consistency.Verification results confirm that the model satisfies these properties, ensuring the reliability of interactions under various scenarios.Furthermore, by incorporating an intruder model and WAMP's optional authentication mechanisms from the Advanced Profile, we demonstrate improved security guarantees.

papers.title: When LLMs Meet Multi-Category Complex Classification: A Comparative Stud
papers.container_title_hint: The 37th International Conference on Software Engineering and Knowledge Engineering, SEKE 2025, KSIR Virtual Conference Center, USA, September 29-30, 2025.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) present new opportunities for tackling complex classification problems; however, few studies have systematically evaluated the performance of LLMs on multi-category classification tasks.This paper conducts a comprehensive comparative analysis of various LLMs and traditional models for complex classification tasks.We made two contributions in this study.First, we provide a systematic experimental evaluation of different models on multi-category classification tasks across both text and vision domains.The models evaluated include four deep learning models (CNN, RNN, ResNet, and EfficientNet), three Transformer models (BERT, ViT, and SwinT), and four LLMs with varying parameter sizes, offering a broad framework to assess model performance in multi-category complex classification.Second, we explore fine-tuning strategies for LLMs and empirically examine the performance of fine-tuned LLMs in text and vision classification tasks.Our results indicate that, without fine-tuning, LLMs do not outperform traditional deep learning and Transformer models in multi-category complex classification when their training knowledge base does not cover the test dataset.However, fine-tuning LLMs can substantially improve their accuracy.We also find that specialized vision Transformer models often achieve higher accuracy than vision LLMs and fine-tuned LLMs.Finally, we share insights and recommendations for future research on LLM-based approaches to complex classification tasks.
